School Media Club Newsletter Draft

Make Our Campus Easier to Navigate

New students often need more time than expected to find classrooms, offices, and activity spaces. During Welcome Week, the Media Club will run three projects to improve campus navigation.

The first project is (1) a photo-map contest. Teams will photograph useful landmarks and create a simple route from the main gate to an assigned destination. The winning maps will be displayed near the entrance and uploaded to the school website.

The second project is a sign-check walk. First, register a team of two or three students. <A> On the day, collect a checklist from the library. <B> Walk through your assigned building and record signs that are missing, unclear, or difficult to see. <C> Submit the checklist and one improvement proposal by 4:30 p.m. <D> The facilities office will review the proposals.

The final project is an information-desk challenge. Students will take turns answering questions from visiting families. (3) Talking to visitors is fun. Participants will learn how to give short, accurate directions and how to check information instead of guessing.

Through these activities, we will be able to (4) become experts at taking photographs. Clear information can reduce stress and help everyone use the campus confidently.

Supervisor comments

(1) Explain the purpose of the photo maps.

(2) Add how the sign-check proposals will be judged.

(3) Replace this with a sentence that connects directly to the learning goal.

(4) Rewrite this so that it summarizes the main argument.

Facilities Office Memo

Proposals will be judged on three points: usefulness for first-time visitors, practicality within the school budget, and clarity of explanation.

Background Information

Last year's orientation survey showed that first-year students most often became lost between the science building, the counseling office, and the gym. International visitors also reported that some directional signs used abbreviations they did not understand. The school cannot replace every sign during one term, so the projects in the newsletter are intended to identify the most urgent improvements and produce temporary guidance while permanent changes are planned.

The Media Club hopes that the activities will not only create useful materials but also teach students to consider information from the reader's point of view. A sign that seems obvious to a current student may be confusing to someone entering the campus for the first time.
